title: Efficient Treatment of Non-Linearity in Quantum Computational Fluid Dynamics Using Hybrid Tensor Networks
authors: Pia Siegl, Nis-Luca van Hülst, Maximilian Mandelt Buxadé, Tomohiro Hashizume, Dieter Jaksch
abstract: Nonlinear terms present a fundamental challenge for quantum computational fluid dynamics, as their implementation on inherently linear quantum hardware typically requires resource-intensive workarounds that limit scalability to large-scale simulations. We present a hybrid quantum-classical tensor network algorithm that addresses this bottleneck by combining variational time-stepping with quantum tensor programming to efficiently compile operators and time-dependent fields into quantum circuits. Within a probabilistic framework, we replace prior state-based nonlinear implementations with tensor-based block encodings, stabilizing success probabilities that otherwise decay exponentially with system size. Benchmarking on turbulent flow fields demonstrates that the algorithm maintains high success probabilities and moderate measurement overhead across increasing Reynolds numbers and grid resolutions. Compared to fully classical tensor network solvers, our hybrid approach yields substantial reductions in both memory footprint and computational cost, establishing a scalable pathway toward practical quantum advantage in scale-resolving CFD simulations.
summary: This paper introduces a novel hybrid quantum-classical algorithm to overcome the major hurdle of nonlinearity in quantum CFD simulations. By using tensor-based block encodings, the method avoids the exponential resource scaling associated with previous state-based approaches. This breakthrough demonstrates a scalable pathway for achieving quantum advantage in simulating complex, high-Reynolds number fluid dynamics.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the efficient and scalable implementation of nonlinear terms within Quantum Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations.
main_result: The proposed hybrid quantum-classical tensor network algorithm significantly reduces the computational cost and memory footprint compared to fully classical tensor network solvers, establishing a scalable path toward quantum advantage in CFD.
method: The authors propose a hybrid approach combining variational time-stepping with quantum tensor programming. Nonlinearity is handled by replacing state-based encodings with tensor-based block encodings, which are compiled into unitary gates.
model_or_system: The study models Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), specifically simulating turbulent flow fields governed by nonlinear Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). Examples include the Temporally Developing Jet (TDJ) and Taylor Green Vortex (TGV).
key_observables: Success probability of the nonlinear operation ($\alpha_{succ}$), computational cost, memory footprint, and the field representation error ($\epsilon_{\ell_2}$).
important_parameters: Reynolds numbers ($Re \in \{10, 20, ..., 1000\}$), bond dimension ($\chi$), and time step ($\Delta t$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that the nonlinear terms can be effectively encoded into diagonal block encodings, which stabilizes the success probability against exponential decay with system size.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the hybrid algorithm workflow, the quantum circuit decomposition for a single time step (distinguishing linear and nonlinear operators), and comparisons of error scaling and computational costs across various Reynolds numbers.
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework for handling nonlinear PDEs using a hybrid quantum-classical loop. It then applies this framework to simulate specific turbulent flow examples (TDJ, TGV), providing rigorous error and cost analyses.
why_interesting: While focused on fluid dynamics, the core methodology—using tensor networks and quantum programming to manage complex, non-linear operators—is highly relevant to simulating open quantum systems or many-body dynamics where nonlinear couplings are present.
